notes: §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR19: "Treatment of a file contained in a multiple file tape environment is logically equivalent to the treatment of a sequential file contained in a single file tape environment." The MULTIPLE FILE TAPE clause is the source text that puts a file in that environment (§1985:VII.2.11.1: "The MULTIPLE FILE TAPE clause specifies the location of files on a multiple file reel."); VisitMultipleFileClause admits it at 85 (COBOL0902 from 2002) and ScreenMultipleFileClause records the membership on FileModel.MultipleFileReels. Nothing in the emitter or the runtime reads that membership: EmitOpen and SequentialConnector.OpenCore open, read, write and close a file of the clause exactly as they do a sequential file no clause names, so the two treatments are the same. The only readers are compile-time screens for rules the standard states apart (CheckOpenModeForFile: OPEN EXTEND, §1985:VII.4.3.3 SR2, and §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR20 d; MERGE's SR6). The clause's own function, the placement of files on a reel, is hardware dependent (§1985:C.3, item 7: "The MULTIPLE FILE TAPE clause is dependent upon a reel type of device.") and not provided (§1985:I.1.5.2.5.1: "Language elements that pertain to specific hardware components for which support is not claimed need not be implemented."; docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 3.4). Probed at --std 85: three files of one clause at POSITION 1, 3 and 5, each assigned its own host file, are written, read back in a different order, opened I-O and rewritten with status 00 throughout; a program whose two files share one implementor-name gives the same output with the clause and with the clause removed. The witness writes two records to a file of the clause and reads them back to the at end condition. Not covered by this verdict: two file-names assigned to one implementor-name are one host file with or without the clause, so the second OPEN OUTPUT replaces the first file's records; POSITION does not separate them (the unprovided reel function).

next.reason: 1985: "Treatment of a file contained in a multiple file tape environment is logically equivalent to the treatment of a sequential file"; 2023: "No OPEN general rule (14.9.27.4 rules 1-26) or file rule mentions a multiple file tape environment". The 2023 OPEN general rules, read in full, have no multiple-file-tape rule, and no file or CLOSE candidate mentions that environment. The feature appears dropped.
